recent_posts.title: News: kea >= 1:3.0.3-6 update requires manual intervention
recent_posts.summary: The kea DHCP server package (version 1:3.0.3-6 and above) has moved all services to run as a dedicated non-root kea user for improved security. Users upgrading from existing installations must manually update file permissions using chown on runtime files under /var/lib/kea, /var/log/kea, and /run/lock/kea, then restart the relevant systemd services. Accounts needing access to kea files should be added to the kea group.

recent_posts.title: News: NVIDIA 590 driver drops Pascal and lower support; main packages switch to Open Kernel Modules
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA driver version 590 discontinues support for Pascal (GTX 10xx) and older GPUs. Arch Linux is transitioning main NVIDIA packages to open kernel modules. Users with Pascal, Maxwell, or older cards must manually switch to the legacy nvidia-580xx-dkms package from AUR to avoid broken graphics. Users with Turing (RTX 20xx, GTX 1650) and newer GPUs will automatically transition to open kernel modules without intervention.

recent_posts.title: News: .NET packages may require manual intervention
recent_posts.summary: .NET packages on Arch Linux upgrading from version 9.0 to 10.0 may encounter dependency errors during installation. Affected packages include aspnet-runtime, dotnet-runtime, and dotnet-sdk. Users needing to keep version 9.0 can manually install versioned packages (e.g., aspnet-runtime-9.0) and remove the unversioned ones using pacman commands.

recent_posts.title: News: dovecot >= 2.4 requires manual intervention
recent_posts.summary: Dovecot 2.4 introduces breaking changes that make it incompatible with 2.3 configuration files, requiring manual migration before the service can start. The replication feature has been removed entirely in 2.4. Arch Linux provides dovecot23 packages as an alternative for users who need the replication feature or cannot migrate immediately. The 2.3 branch will continue receiving critical security fixes.

recent_posts.title: News: Recent service outages
recent_posts.summary: Arch Linux is experiencing ongoing DDoS attacks affecting their main website, AUR, and forums. The project is working with hosting providers to mitigate the attacks and evaluating DDoS protection services. Workarounds are provided for accessing mirrors, ISO images, AUR packages via GitHub, and offline wiki documentation during service disruptions.

recent_posts.title: News: zabbix >= 7.4.1-2 may require manual intervention
recent_posts.summary: Zabbix version 7.4.1-2 on Arch Linux consolidates multiple user accounts (zabbix-server, zabbix-proxy, zabbix-agent, zabbix-web-service) into a single shared 'zabbix' user account through a new zabbix-common package. While main configuration files and systemd services are automatically updated, users must manually update custom files, PSK files, scripts, and sudoers rules that reference the old user accounts to prevent service failures.

recent_posts.title: News: linux-firmware >= 20250613.12fe085f-5 upgrade requires manual intervention
recent_posts.summary: Arch Linux's linux-firmware package version 20250613.12fe085f-5 introduces a breaking change that splits firmware into vendor-focused packages. Due to NVIDIA firmware symlink reorganization, users upgrading from version 20250508.788aadc8-2 or earlier will encounter filesystem conflicts. The solution requires manually removing the old linux-firmware package before performing the system upgrade.

recent_posts.title: News: Plasma 6.4.0 will need manual intervention if you are on X11
recent_posts.summary: KDE Plasma 6.4.0 will default to Wayland-only installation on Arch Linux. Users currently running X11 sessions must manually install plasma-x11-session and kwin-x11 packages to maintain X11 compatibility, as the package manager cannot automatically detect existing session preferences.

recent_posts.title: News: Transition to the new WoW64 wine and wine-staging
recent_posts.summary: Arch Linux is transitioning Wine and wine-staging packages to pure WoW64 builds, removing multilib repository dependencies to align with upstream development. This change simplifies packaging but introduces potential OpenGL performance issues for 32-bit applications and requires recreating existing 32-bit prefixes.

recent_posts.title: News: Valkey to replace Redis in the [extra] Repository
recent_posts.summary: Valkey will replace Redis in the Arch Linux [extra] repository due to Redis changing its license. Arch Linux will support Redis for 14 days to allow a smooth transition to Valkey, after which Redis will be moved to the AUR and will no longer receive updates. Users are advised to switch to Valkey promptly to avoid issues post-transition.

top_posts.title: News: Glibc 2.41 corrupting Discord installation
top_posts.summary: Glibc 2.41's update planned for today may cause a red warning about corrupt installation in the Discord client. This issue is fixed in the Discord canary build. Users who need audio connectivity should use the canary build, browser login, or the flatpak version until the fix is available in the stable release. Chat functionality is not impacted.

top_posts.title: News: The sshd service needs to be restarted after upgrading to openssh-9.8p1
top_posts.summary: After upgrading to openssh-9.8p1, the current SSH daemon will be unable to accept new connections. Restart the sshd service using `systemctl try-restart sshd` immediately after upgrading to resolve the issue. An automatic restart feature is being considered for future releases.

top_posts.title: News: Manual intervention for pacman 7.0.0 and local repositories required
top_posts.summary: Pacman 7.0.0 now supports downloading packages as a separate user with dropped privileges, which may necessitate assigning files to the 'alpm' group and setting executable permissions for users with local repositories. Additionally, there is an improvement in checksum stability for git repositories using .gitattributes, potentially requiring a one-time checksum update for PKGBUILD files.

top_posts.title: Manual pages indexing service
top_posts.summary: A manual pages indexing site at man.archlinux.org that publishes the man pages of all our packages and allows you to search and browse them. You can also find this service linked to in the sidebar as well as on every package detail page. It is our hope that publishing man pages matching the versions of our released packages further improves Arch accessibility.
